mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-73.0, -59.0, -52.3, -37.6), reflecting an accelerating recovery momentum in discretionary mobility. This autoregressive trend is expected to persist, producing a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days than the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased monotonically over the last 4 weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days despite the prior 4-week monotonic uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has recovered from -61.1 to -44.3 over the snapshot window, a sign that transit restrictions or capacity limits are being relaxed. Once TRANSIT crosses above -45, retail trips enabled by public transit access are expected to rise further, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -45 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -61.1 to -44.3 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the 2 weeks following a TRANSIT crossing above -45, or TRANSIT reverses below -50 without RETAIL_REC declining in tandem.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of declining RESIDENTIAL time (24.6 to 14.9) and rising WORKPLACES mobility (-56.3 to -37.3) indicates households are resuming out-of-home routines in a compounding fashion: less home-bound time combined with more commuting generates additional incidental retail trips, amplifying RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series would predict alone.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week while WORKPLACES rises week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined and WORKPLACES rose in every week of the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than the growth predicted from WORKPLACES or RESIDENTIAL alone, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility turned positive and accelerated from -20.9 to 19.3 across the snapshot, consistent with a seasonal shift toward warmer-weather outdoor activity. In this seasonal regime, outdoor errands and park-adjacent retail (dining, outdoor shopping) co-occur, so continued PARKS gains should coincide with further RETAIL_REC increases over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -20.9 to 19.3 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 4 weeks even as PARKS continues its positive trajectory, or PARKS plateaus/declines while RETAIL_REC keeps rising, breaking the co-movement.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near baseline (-10.0), suggesting essential-trip demand is saturated and any further mobility gains will spill into discretionary retail. Combined with the recent RETAIL_REC uptrend, this saturation should push RETAIL_REC higher over the coming week as consumers substitute essential trips for discretionary ones.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within 5 points of its prior week value (saturation)
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM change slowed from -18.0 to -13.4 to -10.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stays flat over the next week despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining saturated near -10.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -35 percent change from baseline, this signals a formal reopening of office-based employment, which historically drives a surge in lunch-hour and after-work retail trips within 2 weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -35 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -37.3 at t-0w, approaching the -35 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 2 weeks after WORKPLACES crosses above -35, or the crossing does not occur and RETAIL_REC still rises, disconfirming the causal link.

mechanism_narrative: The rate of improvement in RETAIL_REC is decelerating in absolute terms (gains of 14.0, 6.7, 14.7 points per week after an initial 14-point jump), suggesting behavioral fatigue or a ceiling effect as pent-up demand is exhausted. This deceleration pattern implies the next 4-week mean will show a smaller or negative increment relative to the prior 4-week mean, i.e., RETAIL_REC may plateau or dip.
candidate_trigger: week-on-week RETAIL_REC gain falls below 5 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise at a rate equal to or greater than the prior 4-week average, showing no deceleration or plateau.

mechanism_narrative: In a seasonal regime where PARKS mobility has turned positive while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above 10 points, outdoor-oriented households still spend disproportionate time at home outside of park visits, limiting spillover into retail within the immediate next week; this combination caps near-term RETAIL_REC gains until RESIDENTIAL falls further.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remains at 14.9 while PARKS is at 19.3
regime_hint: early-season outdoor transition with elevated residential time
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week even though RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 points, contradicting the proposed cap on retail spillover.
